transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Evan Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Quantaco VP Eng), Priya Singh (Quantaco ML Eng Manager), Sara Gomez (Quantaco Infra Lead), Noah Kim (SRE)

Summary:
Quick cost/unit economics review for the ongoing POC. Focus on tokens/sec per dollar, caching savings observed, batching tradeoffs, and next steps to run longer steady-state benchmarks and a dedicated canary on NGC instances. Some audio artifacts and a couple of mis-transcribed product names (we heard 'KeyV cache' once).

Topics:
- Recent benchmark results (tokens/sec/$)
- Cache hit rates and expected savings with longer TTLs
- Batching: latency vs throughput tradeoffs and tail latency concerns
- Dedicated vs hosted routing for production
- Next steps and owners

[00:00] Evan Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in today, same agenda as before — cost econ, caching, batching. Priya, you ok to kick us off with the numbers from last week's run?

[00:18] Priya Singh: Yeah hi, thanks. so we ran the 8 hour run on the staging cluster, mixed seq lengths 32/128/512, with our normal traffic mix. overall tokens per second improved about 22% when we enabled prefix caching with the TTL at 15 minutes. cost per 1M tokens dropped roughly 18% in our estimate. uh, caveat is we saw a small bump in 95th pctile latency for short seq requests when batching was aggressive.

[00:45] Maya Patel: When you say batching was aggressive, what's your target batch size and max latency?

[00:50] Priya Singh: We had batch target 64, max wait 40ms. most flows hit batch sizes 40-60 in the steady window. the short seq 32 requests occasionally hit the 95th at 220ms vs baseline 180ms. so tail went up ~40ms.

[01:12] Liam O'Connor: Is that acceptable for our live product? our latency SLO for user-facing is 200ms p95. so that is a bit concerning.

[01:20] Evan Chen: Right, that's exactly the tradeoff — batching for unit cost vs p95 latency. One idea is to use two routes: a low-latency route with batch target 8 and a high-throughput route for background/async jobs. Redwood supports that routing policy today.

[01:36] Noah Kim: Quick Q — what's the cache hit rate you saw? Priya?

[01:40] Priya Singh: average hit rate 28% on the prefix/KV cache. when we extended TTL from 5 to 15 minutes it climbed from ~18% to 28%. we think with small changes in prompt templating we can push to mid-30s. That translates to an estimated 12-20% cost reduction depending on overlap.

[02:00] Maya Patel: Those numbers align with what we see in other customers — small TTL increases give outsized benefits if traffic has reuse. Couple notes: Redwood's cache is prefix-aware and will serve KV hits without recompute for compatible variants; but if you do many short personalized prefixes the hit rate drops.

[02:19] Sara Gomez: Our personalization is small — user id + few tokens. we try to keep templates identical. the problem is session affinity; some requests come from ephemeral sessions so TTL 15m might be optimistic for some flows.

[02:35] Priya Singh: yeah we saw that, the session-limited flows had sub 10% hit. but non-personalized flows like help queries were 45% hit.

[02:45] Evan Chen: ok so there's clear value in nudging more requests into the cached template path. For the cost model I updated the spreadsheet to incorporate both caching savings and batching effects. I can share after this — it shows tokens/sec per dollar under different configs: hosted default, hosted with caching, dedicated with quant/8-bit, and dedicated + batching.

[03:05] Liam O'Connor: can you summarize the delta between hosted vs dedicated in simple terms? like % savings per 1M tokens?

[03:10] Evan Chen: Roughly, for your workload profile, hosted default is baseline. With caching and moderate batching you get ~18-25% cost reduction. Dedicated with same configs and quantization gets you an additional ~20-30% depending on hardware and utilization. so total potential savings up to ~40-50% in favorable cases. again these are estimates, we should validate with a dedicated benchmark.

[03:32] Priya Singh: important note — dedup and caching interact with quantization — some kernels behave differently at 8-bit; we saw a couple of small quality diffs in edge cases but nothing major. will need evals.

[03:45] Maya Patel: yes, quality monitoring is key. we'll tie evaluation prompts to the regression alerts in Redwood Optimize so you get automatic flags if generation quality drifts after quant/patch.

[03:55] Noah Kim: question on tokens/sec/$ — how are you measuring tokens? do you include prompt+response or just response tokens?

[04:02] Evan Chen: Good — the spreadsheet uses total tokens (prompt + response) since your prompt sizes are non-trivial. we can show both if you'd prefer. the important metric is end-to-end cost per API call and tokens/sec throughput at target latency.

[04:18] Priya Singh: also we noticed cache priming costs initially — the first hour of warm-up looked worse because cache warm-up takes time. in steady-state after 3 hours cost per token stabilized lower. that's why we recommended a 24h run.

[04:32] Liam O'Connor: That makes sense. we want to see steady-state numbers.

[04:36] Evan Chen: On batching tradeoffs — you can set adaptive policies: prefer low-latency for interactive routes, and high-batch for bulk inference. Redwood supports dynamic routing by traffic class, plus autoscaling so dedicated pools don't blow utilization.

[04:52] Sara Gomez: about autoscaling — we need to see how sudden spikes affect p95 if we scale too slowly. we prefer predictable capacity for major spikes, which might push us towards Reserved Dedicated for the busiest endpoints.

[05:05] Maya Patel: We can configure reserved capacity with a burst pool. For the POC we can run a dedicated small pool to emulate reserved capacity and capture spike behavior. that's one of the canary steps I proposed.

[05:20] Priya Singh: On the sample numbers, can you add a column in the spreadsheet that shows assumed utilization? we ran into big differences between 40% and 80% utilization in your prior sheet.

[05:30] Evan Chen: Absolutely — I'll add utilization slices 30/50/70/90% and show unit cost at each. also I'll include sensitivity to cache hit rate (10/25/40%) and batching target (8/32/64).

[05:45] Liam O'Connor: One more question — security/compliance: if we move to private deployment or VPC, how does that affect cost and operations?

[05:54] Evan Chen: Private and VPC deployments incur platform fees and you'll manage networking; operationally you get isolated control plane, KMS integration, audit logs. Cost delta is mostly infra and support — for large scale it often pays off given the unit savings, but we can model it in the spreadsheet too.

[06:12] Priya Singh: ok thanks. for next steps I think we agree on a 24 hour steady-state run with caching enabled and a dedicated canary run on NGC with kernel traces.

[06:22] Evan Chen: yep. to recap action items: Priya run the 24h steady-state; Maya set up canary on NGC; Evan to share updated cost model; Sara to share request distribution. we'll reconvene next week — same time?

[06:36] Liam O'Connor: yes same time next week works for us.

[06:40] Jordan Lee: I'll drop the meeting invite and add the slide deck + links to the cost spreadsheet and security docs in the calendar.

[06:48] Evan Chen: Great. anything else from the Quantaco side?

[06:52] Priya Singh: no, that's all. thanks.

[06:55] Evan Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up.

[07:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard product names ("KeyV cache" vs KV cache), some timestamps approximate. References shared: cost_model_qc_v3.xlsx (link in calendar), benchmark logs (s3://quantaco-poc/logs), Redwood security whitepaper (link).

Recap / Next steps (brief):
- Evan: share cost model + revised spreadsheet with utilization & cache/batch sensitivity by 2026-03-31
- Priya: run 24h steady-state benchmark with caching TTL 15m and capture p95/p99 by 2026-04-06
- Maya: schedule NGC dedicated canary and collect kernel traces, provide summary slides by 2026-04-02
- Sara: share production request distribution slice (seq lengths, prefix reuse %) by 2026-04-01

End of transcript.
